correctness.rationale: In the specified two-/three-subset inclusion graph, a selected pair passes exactly when deleting the other selected vertices does not increase its distance. An independent blocked-BFS census generated all feasible sets up to the first empty layer (size nine); pruning by infeasible subsets is exact by heredity. It reproduced (1,20,190,1080,3925,8944,11300,5840,150), the total 31,450, and facet counts (60,4700,150) at sizes (6,7,8) by testing all one-vertex extensions. It verified the two optimum orbits of sizes 30 and 120 under the 240 label permutations and complement operations, including their stated induced types. Independently, on one shore a disjoint selected pair has distance four and its geodesics use a middle shore vertex consisting of one label from each endpoint. If omissions intersect, by relabelling they are 01 and 02, and the pair 12,34 has all four such intermediates selected. If the omissions are disjoint, they cannot both avoid crossing between the two chosen disjoint endpoints: neither equals an endpoint and both would need the fifth label. Thus a pure optimum corresponds exactly to an omitted Petersen edge. The checked optimum exchanges identify precisely two copies of the line graph, with no edges to the mixed optima. The line graphs have diameter three (the Petersen graph has diameter two, and the edges (01,23) and (02,13) have all cross-endpoint distances two). Within a shore no exchange is a slide because the original graph is bipartite. All 150 optima are therefore slide-frozen.
residual_risks: The census is exhaustive on this fixed labelled graph, not on all middle-level graphs. The movement result fixes cardinality eight and does not address routes through suboptimal configurations.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a natural symmetric incidence graph. Its precise optimum structure sharply separates the two movement rules: every optimum is slide-frozen, while jumps have two nontrivial components naturally indexed by Petersen edges and 120 isolated optima. This gives an exact structural benchmark that a maximum, or even the complete face polynomial alone, does not provide. The separate facet census records maximal configurations smaller than the optimum.
residual_risks: The value is a complete single-graph classification, not an asserted general reconfiguration theorem.
